Q: Get filepath using Flet in python A:

The issue you're running into is a common security "gotcha" with modern web and desktop frameworks. For security reasons, Flet (and the underlying browsers/engines) won't give you the full local path (like C:\Users\Documents\file.xlsx) because that reveals the user's file system structure.

However, since you want to process this in Pandas or Polars without saving to a temporary directory, you can achieve this by using the on_result event of the FilePicker and accessing the file's bytes directly.

Here is the updated, idiomatic way to handle this in current Flet versions:

The Solution: Using Bytes in Memory

Instead of looking for a path, you should let the FilePicker upload the file to a memory buffer. You can then pass those bytes directly into pd.read_excel() or pl.read_excel().

Python

import flet as ft
import pandas as pd
import io

async def main(page: ft.Page):
    page.title = "File Picker to Pandas"
    
    # 1. Define the handler first
    async def on_file_result(e: ft.FilePickerResultEvent):
        if e.files:
            # We take the first file
            picked_file = e.files[0]
            
            # For local desktop apps, 'path' might work, 
            # but for true cross-platform/web, use bytes:
            # Note: upload_files() is required if you're on web, 
            # but for standalone desktop, you can often read directly if permitted.
            
            # Direct approach for standalone desktop:
            try:
                # If path is available, use it; otherwise, we'd use the upload strategy
                df = pd.read_excel(picked_file.path)
                selected_files.value = f"Loaded {picked_file.name}. Rows: {len(df)}"
            except Exception as ex:
                selected_files.value = f"Error: {str(ex)}"
            
            page.update()

    # 2. Initialize the Picker and add to page overlay
    file_picker = ft.FilePicker(on_result=on_file_result)
    page.overlay.append(file_picker)

    selected_files = ft.Text()

    # 3. Trigger the picker
    async def handle_upload_click(e):
        await file_picker.pick_files(
            file_type=ft.FilePickerFileType.CUSTOM,
            allowed_extensions=['xlsx']
        )

    page.add(
        ft.Row(
            controls=[
                ft.ElevatedButton(
                    "UPLOAD",
                    icon=ft.icons.UPLOAD_FILE,
                    on_click=handle_upload_click
                ),
                selected_files,
            ],
            alignment=ft.MainAxisAlignment.CENTER
        )
    )

ft.app(target=main)

Key Changes Explained:

  • page.overlay.append(file_picker): In recent Flet versions, the FilePicker is a non-visual control that must be added to the page.overlay to function correctly.

  • FilePickerResultEvent: The e.files object contains a list of SelectedFile objects. These have a .path property. On Desktop (standalone), this path is usually the absolute path.

  • Memory Alternative: If you were on the Web, .path would be None. In that case, you would use file_picker.upload_files() and then process the file via a FastAPI/Flask backend or bytes. But for your standalone requirement, the .path property should work as long as the OS grants permission.

A Note on Polars

If you are using Polars, simply swap the pandas line:

Python

import polars as pl
df = pl.read_excel(picked_file.path)

Q: Is there a concept in python 3 which integrates with the while statement like an iterator does with the for statement? A:

I don't want to put words in user19077881's mouth, but I think they mean that by using the Walrus operator you call the len function only once:

my_list = [1, 2, 3, 4]
prev_length = -1

while (length := len(my_list)) != prev_length:
    prev_length = length
    if length:
        print(my_list.pop())

Q: Situations where R strips attributes for S3 classes, and how to work around or avoid them? A:

I think your design (keeping the text version as the value) is the right design, but you need to warn your users that they should avoid using ifelse() and other functions (e.g. c()) that strip attributes on those objects.

If you think functions like those will be needed but don't want to require the dplyr or data.table packages, then provide your own versions, e.g.

ifelse_tinypval <- function(test, yes, no) {
    stopifnot(inherits(yes, "tinypval"), inherits(no, "tinypval"))
    make_tinypval(ifelse(test, yes, no))
}

If you're worried that people will mistakenly use the class-dropping functions anyway, then add lots of stopifnot(inherits(..., "tinypval")) tests to your own functions to detect when the class has been dropped.

Q: hive reach max worker and cannot connect to hiveserver2 A:

It works fine on my environment:

$ netstat -an | grep 10000
tcp4       0      0  *.10000                *.*                    LISTEN
  • hive-site.xml

set nosasl for not using SASLTransport

<property>
    <name>hive.server2.authentication</name>
    <value>NOSASL</value> <!-- default NONE is for SASLTranspor
</property>

 <property>
    <name>hive.server2.enable.doAs</name>
    <value>false</value> <!-- Execute query as hiveserver2 proc
</property>

and 

!connect jdbc:hive2://localhost:10000/default;auth=noSasl hive password org.apache.hive.jdbc.HiveDriver
